Claude working notes for IsaacUre.github.io

Workflow

  • When a task on a feature branch is complete, automatically create a PR against main (if one does not already exist for the branch) and squash-merge it. The user has standing approval for auto-merge on this repo.
  • If the branch already has a prior merged PR at an older commit, open a new PR for the new commits and squash-merge that.
  • Never commit a test harness or scratch file to the repo root. The repo is served at isaacure.com. Dotfolders are committed but never published.

NINTH NIGHT

The game at /tcomp/ (tcomp/ninth.js). It is being built out by several chats working in parallel. It is not in /comp/, the public cut (see tcomp below): the job docs, the harness pages and every path in them mean /tcomp/.

If asked to "do ninth night job N", read .claude/ninth-night/JOBS.md and then that job's file. Read .claude/ninth-night/README.md and PARALLEL.md first either way: PARALLEL.md says which parts of the file your job owns and which shared structures have registries instead of being edited directly.

.claude/ninth-night/TESTING.md is the harness playbook. The short version: drive the game with real key events, not the window.__ninth dev handle, because a build once shipped where pressing E did nothing and the dev handle reported everything working.

tcomp

/comp/ is the public cut of the computer; /tcomp/ is the full build. /comp/ is what the site links to and the one being polished for release, so it ships without Steam (and the games that only ran through it: Cookie Clicker, Terraria, VEILFALL, Sunset Runner), without Minecraft (the launcher and the game), without NINTH NIGHT, and without the Edge gag: Chrome is simply installed, pinned to the taskbar and Start, with a desktop shortcut. /tcomp/ still has all of it, at isaacure.com/tcomp, to try things on before they move to /comp/.

  • The lore those games left in the file system is out of /comp/ too, and comes back with them. All of it still exists in tcomp/comp.js's file tree: Documents\My Games\Terraria (and the wld and plr file kinds), Documents\essays\absurdism and idle games.txt, the Terraria and Cookie Clicker screenshots in Pictures\Screenshots and captures in Videos\Captures, minecraft worlds backup under D:\archive\old laptop (2016-2019)\games, the seed line at the end of the secret.txt on D:, NINTH NIGHT's folder under C:\Program Files\URE Softworks, and the Cookie Clicker chip on Chrome's Wikipedia page.
  • The two directories are not interchangeable: cp tcomp/* comp/ would bring everything back. Move a change across file by file, or as a patch. Both index.htmls load their scripts and stylesheet by relative path (comp.js, not /comp/comp.js); keep it that way, since an absolute /comp/ or /tcomp/ in a loader tag makes one copy silently run the other's code.
  • The saves are shared. Both copies sit on one origin and read and write the same localStorage keys, so a test build shares its saves with the live one.
  • The NINTH NIGHT docs and every harness under .claude/ point at /tcomp/; nothing they drive is in /comp/ any more. The QC logs in .claude/ninth-night/qc-2026-08-12/ still say comp/ because they are a record, not instructions.
  • Minecraft's sounds are the real game's own recordings, as files in tcomp/mc-sounds/ (83 MB, most of it the soundtrack). More, already encoded the same way, wait in this repo's mc-sounds-archive release; .claude/comp-tools/mc-sounds/README.md says how to add one, where the full original archive is, and how to check. minecraft.js loads them from beside its own script, so a copy of the game in /comp/ would need its own mc-sounds/ beside it.
  • Its textures, interface sprites, font glyphs and title wordmark are the game's own too, in tcomp/mc-tex/, built from a Minecraft client jar by .claude/comp-tools/mc-tex/build.py (its README says how, and what each file is). Anything missing there falls back to the drawings in minecraft.js. Block faces in the world are taken down from 16 to 12 texels on purpose (Isaac asked for a slightly more pixel look); WTEX in minecraft.js sets it.
  • Its screens follow Java 26.3, read out of the jar's class files with .claude/comp-tools/mc-tex/jdis.py (the README there says how). The Game Menu's World Options... holds the LAN scope and the world's Allow Cheats (26.3 has no Open to LAN screen); the mc-play/creative.js suite drives it.

test

/test/ is the face of the site being built: a "who is this guy" page in the holding page's look (the same boot terminal, and the same LCD, which now types the name and whoami). It lives at isaacure.com/test until Isaac moves it to the root. (It was at /new/ at first; that path is gone, not redirected.)

  • It stays unlisted until he says otherwise: noindex, nofollow, no canonical or og:url, and no link to it from anywhere on the site. Drop the noindex when it moves.
  • Every fact on it is one he has confirmed or published himself. Ask him before adding a biographical claim (a date, a title, a number), and don't copy one from comp/, ureboy/ or behind-the-lens/: the computer is half lore, and the other two still carry old dates.
  • The screen stays alive the way the holding page's does: its eye blinks twice every 8s and its cursor (and Contact's) keeps blinking. Isaac asked for that over WCAG 2.2.2's five-second rule, so don't "fix" it. Everything else settles within five seconds of the boot's hand-off, and without JS or under reduced motion it is simply the finished page, with nothing moving.
  • The About pictures each have a little move (PICS in the script, drawn in frames like the blink). Each plays once when all of it comes into view, again on hover or tap, and again when you come back after 20s. They never loop.
  • Stepped animations that fill backwards use end steps (or none): a start step filled backwards shows its first frame during the delay in browsers without the easing spec's "before flag". That is how the name once showed its I before typing it.
  • It loads everything by absolute path (/images/..., /favicon.svg), so moving it to the root is a copy.
  • There is no section for the rest of the site. Isaac took the "This site" one out and may add one back later (it would be the place for comp/ and 1p/). GitHub is off the Contact list on purpose until he has a GitHub he wants to show; don't put it back unless he asks.
  • .claude/test/rig/ has its checks (170 of them, plus axe and html-validate). Run them after any change; its README says how.

test2

/test2/ is the same page as /test/ rebuilt as a Windows 11 desk of Windows Terminal windows: the holding page's boot hands off to a desk with a taskbar along the bottom, and every part of the page is a Windows Terminal window (the tab row with its one tab, the caption buttons at the right, VT323 inside) running PowerShell 7, each of which ran one command: a login shell that prints PowerShell 7.6.7 and the banner and answers whoami, fastfetch with the eye for a logo, chafa headshot.jpg, type readme.md, dir interests -Name and a type for each, Import-Csv log.csv and a type for each line, and type contact.txt. It lives at isaacure.com/test2 until Isaac picks one of the two. The chrome follows Windows Terminal's source (the 40px tab row, the tab filled with the terminal's black, the 46px caption buttons and their colours, Campbell's #0c0c0c, the bar cursor) and PowerShell's (the PowerShell 7.6.7 line, the default prompt, the aliases type, dir, start, Import-Csv); the cream taskbar, the red accent frame and the palette inside are the page's own choices, not Windows'.

  • Everything in ## test holds here too: unlisted (noindex, nofollow, no canonical or og:url, no link to it), only facts he has confirmed (the copy is /test/'s, word for word; the file names, the prompt, the version and the window titles are chrome, not facts), absolute paths, the loops kept (fastfetch's eye blinks on the 8s loop, the front window's cursor blinks), everything else still within five seconds, and the finished page with nothing moving under reduced motion or without JS. GitHub stays off the contact list.
  • The prompt is PowerShell's default, PS C:\Users\isaac> , all of it dim. The windows' titles are plain names (whoami, fastfetch, readme.md, log\rice-racing.md, contact.txt); paths use backslashes; the command is the first line inside, and /test/'s section titles are comments at the prompt above it (# who is this guy, # effectively mini resume, # say hi). Prompt lines are aria-hidden decoration except where they hold a link or Isaac's words (the comments, with the # hidden). The next prompt follows the output on the very next line; the only blank lines are the ones in the files and the ones the csv's table prints around itself. The log entries' # Org lines are h3s under the window's h2.
  • The caption buttons are Windows': Minimize, Maximize, Close at the right of the tab row, 46px wide and the row's full height, with 10px glyphs; Maximize alone is a toggle (aria-pressed) and only its glyph changes to restore. The front window has the accent frame (Tornado Red), a #2e2e2e row, white glyphs and the only cursor; a window at the back has a #333333 row, grey glyphs and no cursor (Windows Terminal hides an unfocused terminal's cursor). The tab is filled with the terminal's black and runs into the body; the + and v after it are drawn and inert.
  • Two things break by the window's width, not the viewport's (container queries, with a viewport query as the fallback): fastfetch puts the eye above the facts in a window under 348px, and the banner breaks into its two words, URE under ISAAC, the way figlet wraps, in one under 310px. The + and v go in a window under 420px.
  • The windows are a CSS grid (twelve columns on a desktop, six on a tablet, one on a phone) with a whole-pixel nudge each (--nx, --ny) so they overlap at the edges. The script only adds behaviour: the cascade (what is in view pops in order and lights up in turn; the rest when scrolled to, without taking the front), raise on click, drag by the tab row with a mouse (never a finger, a touchscreen laptop's included: a finger scrolls), minimize to the taskbar (the window shrinks toward its taskbar button and keeps its place on the desk, unseen; on a phone it is simply gone; its section's taskbar button, the window list, a link to it or Reset brings it back), maximize (Maximize again, a double-click on the row or Escape restores; the rest goes inert), close (the grid reflows), and the eye's window list in the taskbar, which also resets the desk. The login shell is the front window at rest (after the cascade, after a reset, and under reduced motion), so its cursor is the one blinking.
  • The taskbar is Windows 11's in the LCD's cream: Start (the eye) and a labelled button per part of the page in the middle, the tray and the two-line clock at the right, the running indicator under a part with windows up and the long accent one under the part you are in (aria-current, set by scroll: home while the login shell's top half is on screen, the part in the upper half of the screen below that, contact at the bottom). As it narrows, in ems, it moves left and loses the tray, then the icons and the date, then the clock; the labels always stay. The skip link goes to the taskbar, the one thing after the windows. The window list is a flyout up from Start with a row per window and its state in words.
  • The boot terminal is .term; a terminal window is .win. Don't reuse the boot's class for a window: its rule once leaked onto every terminal window (16px text, touch-action: none).
  • Its boot flag is iu2.booted, its own, so a visit to /test/ in the same session doesn't skip it.
  • .claude/test2/rig/ has its checks (the probe, axe, html-validate, the screenshots). Run them after any change; its README says how. The fonts come from .claude/test/rig/fonts.

tcomp Minecraft: the game's own sounds and C418's soundtrack replace the synth (#165)

* Minecraft: the game's own sounds and C418's soundtrack replace the synth

Every sound in the tcomp Minecraft was synthesized from oscillators and
noise. It now plays Minecraft's real samples from tcomp/mc-sounds/: 378
effects and 25 music tracks, AAC at 96 kbps, 83 MB. They come from a
fan-kept archive of the game's sound folder, checked for malware first.

- Block SoundTypes, mob voices and one-shot events are sample tables
  with the game's own volume and pitch maths. Stand-ins become the real
  sounds: bucket fill and empty, milking, tilling, armor equip per tier,
  the egg plop, the enderman's stare and scream, drowning and fire hurt,
  the HUD bubble pop, the lightning strike.
- New, because the game has them: mob footsteps, slime jump, squish and
  attack, squid ambience, underwater enter and exit over the underwater
  bed, rain as scattered clips, menu music on the title screen.
- Gone, because the game is silent there: the bow-draw creak, the bed
  whoosh, the creeper's death puff (it has a real death sound now).
- Effects are padded before encoding and trimmed at load against a
  calibration pulse, so every browser starts them on time. Music streams
  through an <audio> element, its moov box moved to the front.
- .claude/comp-tools/mc-sounds/ holds the build (Windows' own AAC
  encoder) and a headless-Edge check suite; serve.js now serves byte
  ranges and audio/mp4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* mc-sounds tools: leave nothing running or lying around

The check suite now closes Edge through the protocol, which takes its
renderer, GPU and utility processes with it; killing only the browser
process left them running, a few hundred MB a run. build.py deletes its
padded WAVs when it finishes.

* tcomp Minecraft: the game's own textures, font, sprites and sky

Everything the game draws now comes from the Minecraft 26.3 client jar,
built into tcomp/mc-tex/ by .claude/comp-tools/mc-tex/build.py: blocks,
items, crops, particles, the interface sprites, the font and the enchanting

- The sun and moon are the game's size (30 and 20 at 100), added onto the
  sky; the moon's phase follows a day count that the tick and /time keep.
- The cactus is the game's 14-wide shape; cracks are blended, not
  alpha-tested; system toasts use the game's card, wrapped at 200.
- The first-person arm wears the launcher's skin, like the inventory figure.
- pwshim drives the installed Edge where Playwright is absent, so the
  mc-play suites run with nothing to install.

root: the boot runs about 40% quicker, and the screen settles sooner (#161)

The terminal boot's holds and slides are roughly halved: the lone
cursor holds 120ms instead of 250, the checks land sooner (power 30,
memcheck 60, the clock 15, /site 90, the eye subsystem 50), the banner
holds 120, and the eye's first look, its glance and its last look are
quicker. The eye's one blink keeps the LCD's timing. The scripted boot
is about 1.9s instead of 3.2s.

On the screen, the power-on surge and the eye opening are shorter,
COMING SOON types at 30ms a glyph instead of 45, and the glance, the
